notable.note: Short internal call, unusually high value for the audit. Five things. (1) A qualification override is stated openly: the setter flags a 23-year-old as doubtful on financial qualification and lets him through anyway — 'the fact that he's 23 did make me question financial qualification a bit, but, as Chris was saying earlier, he was such a good fit, I thought I'd let it slide, and either way, I think we'll get him through on the primal year.' Direct evidence that ICP income screening is being waived at the setter stage with a cheaper tier as the fallback. (2) A scripted misrepresentation: a lead who asked to see plan options in writing was told 'we don't have a standard menu of plans. It's all custom', when this batch alone shows fixed tiers at $6,000/6mo, $4,000/3mo, $3,000 with Caden, $1,000/6mo self-study and $200/mo. (3) Closers are presented to leads as 'advisors'; the rep is relaxed about it — 'if they know I'm a closer, they can just tell I'm a closer, it doesn't matter'. (4) The rep describes a prospect from the previous day, Jeffrey, as 'a little of a weirdo' shortly after telling him on the call 'let's get you started tomorrow'. (5) The rep pre-empts his own loss reason unprompted: 'maybe he's like, well, Richard was too pushy. I would be surprised if that would be his reason' — worth reading against the Rudolph and Geoffrey calls, where he re-asked for payment repeatedly after being declined. Also: Kim Forbes-Sobers is referred to as 'he' both here and on the Edward Garcia call, which may matter for identity resolution. A team member named Chris is referenced and is not one of the three coded setters.
